c.tagline: South Africa's warm-water playground of golden surf beaches and spice.

taxi.fareNote: Street-hailed metered taxis are uncommon; most visitors use Uber or Bolt, which are cheap and widely available. Agree a fare in advance for any non-app taxi.

emergency.note: 112 works from any mobile phone (free, no airtime needed) and connects to police, fire, and ambulance; 10111 is the national police line and 10177 the ambulance line.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Caution in the CBD/Point and on the beachfront at night; muggings — stay in patrolled tourist zones

hood_desc: Durban's beachfront spine along the Indian Ocean, an 8km promenade of gold-sand surf beaches, hotels, piers, and Moses Mabhida Stadium; best for first-time visitors who want the sea, uShaka Marine World, and the classic Durban holiday feel on their doorstep.

The buzzing heart of Durban nightlife and dining, a jacaranda-lined avenue in the affluent Morningside suburb packed with trendy bars, upscale restaurants, coffee shops, boutiques, and elegant guesthouses; suits travelers who want to eat and go out within walking distance.

An upmarket coastal resort town just north of the city with sandy beaches, a landmark lighthouse, the huge Gateway shopping mall, and a strip of restaurants and hotels; great for a relaxed, safer-feeling beach base with modern amenities.

A leafy ridge suburb overlooking the city and harbour, home to grand old homes, Mitchell Park, and quick access to both the CBD and Morningside; a convenient, more residential mid-range base close to the action.

A bohemian, tree-lined student and creative quarter near the university, filled with craft cafes, art galleries, antique shops, and easygoing eateries; suits younger travelers and those wanting a laid-back, local, budget-friendly vibe.

water.note: Municipal tap water is treated and generally safe, though supply issues in some suburbs make bottled a cautious backup.

transit.hours: The People Mover runs roughly 5:00am-11:30pm daily on 15-30 min frequencies; municipal buses run early morning to mid-evening with little or no late-night service.
transit.note: Most visitors stick to the People Mover loop along the beachfront and CBD plus Uber/Bolt; the informal minibus taxis are cheap and used widely by locals but hard for newcomers to navigate, and the GO!Durban BRT network is still being rolled out.
transit.pay: The People Mover and municipal buses use a reloadable MUVO smartcard (tap on board) or cash; fares are low, roughly R6-20 (~$0.40-1.20) per trip. Minibus taxis take cash only.

bus: Durban Station (Intercape, Greyhound, City to City)

transit.m: Airport shuttle bus (King Shaka Airbus / Margate Coaches) to city (~45-60 min)
Metered taxi or Uber/Bolt to the beachfront (~35 min)

tip.r: ~10-15% at restaurants (rarely included in the bill); cash is preferred, and a few rand for car guards and porters is customary.
